text:
maria: Heads-up — reconciliation job we kicked off for default-permissions just flagged ~1.2k users who lost write perms on `projects`. Not all in the same orgs.

alex.k: ugh. Is this the new role_id migration backfill? which run?

maria: the nightly backfill from last night (migration-service v3.4.1). It attempted to map legacy default_role -> default_v2. We see a mix of `null` and duplicate role ids in users.

samir: quick query I ran: 
```sql
SELECT u.id, u.default_role_id, r.name
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN roles r ON r.id = u.default_role_id
WHERE r.name IS NULL OR r.name LIKE 'default%';
```
returned ~1.2k rows with role_id pointing to a deleted/soft-deleted role.

irene: any audit logs showing the migration writes? can we see the exact payload?

rbac-bot: 2026-03-19T22:10:34Z | svc:migration-service | action:update_user | user_id:81234 | old_role:default | new_role:default_v2 | tx:0x9a1c | status:OK

maria: noted that audit line. But for a subset status=OK while the role_id referenced a role that was later soft-deleted by another cleanup job. Concurrency/race between cleanup and backfill.

alex.k: sounds like we need two fixes: 1) make the backfill idempotent and resilient to soft-deletes (lookup by name and recreate if missing), 2) add a DB-level protection so users can't point to a soft-deleted role id.

samir: agreed. immediate mitigation: rolling back the backfill is risky. Instead we can run a reconciliation that: 
1) identifies users with invalid role_id 
2) sets them to canonical `default_v2` by name (create if missing) 
3) emit a compact audit record so support can notify affected customers.

maria: proposed SQL for step 2 (idempotent): 
```sql
INSERT INTO roles (name, attrs, created_at)
VALUES ('default_v2', '{}', now())
ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET attrs = roles.attrs RETURNING id;

WITH canonical AS (
  SELECT id FROM roles WHERE name = 'default_v2'
)
UPDATE users u
SET default_role_id = (SELECT id FROM canonical)
WHERE u.default_role_id IS NULL OR u.default_role_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM roles WHERE deleted_at IS NULL);
```

irene: also suggest adding a foreign key + partial index to prevent pointing at deleted roles: 
```sql
ALTER TABLE users
ADD CONSTRAINT fk_users_default_role
FOREIGN KEY (default_role_id) REFERENCES roles(id)
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL; -- pseudo, some DBs don't support this directly
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON roles (name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```
This will stop future races.

alex.k: For rollout: can we gate the reconciliation behind a feature-flag and run in dry-run for 1h? I want to see delta counts before we touch prod.

maria: yes. Migration-service already has a --dry-run mode. I'll run dry-run and post counts.

rbac-bot: DRY-RUN REPORT: identified 1247 users with invalid role_id; candidates for reassignment: 1247; would create role default_v2: true

maria: OK. plan: 
- run dry-run (maria) now, post results 
- if numbers match, schedule reconciliation window tomorrow 02:00 UTC (low traffic) with irene oncall + samir DB standby + alex deploy approval
- patch migration code to upsert by name and retry on FK errors (alex)
- add uniqueness constraint on roles.name where deleted_at IS NULL (samir)

alex.k: I'll prepare the migration patch and a quick smoke test script. Also add an alert on audit log anomalies (migration writes where role id not found).

samir: after reassignment we'll keep an immutable audit entry for each user changed so support can trace and rollback if needed. prefix = MIGRATION-RECONCILE-2026-03-20

irene: can SRE reserve a single DB connection and run the update inside a small transaction batch to avoid long locks? we don't want table-wide locks.

maria: we'll do batched updates (1k rows per tx) with backoff. I'll post the runbook snippet in #incidents once scheduled.

alex.k: one more safety: add a temporary feature flag that makes the app treat missing role_id as default_v2 at runtime (reads only) for 48h post-reconcile, to avoid user-facing 403s while users propagate.

maria: good call. I'll coordinate with product for comms if we need to message customers.

rbac-bot: ACTIONS: dry-run done -> 1247; schedule tentative window 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC; owners: maria, alex.k, samir, irene.

maria: thanks all. I'll post the final runbook + SQL and the exact deploy checklist in ~30m. :thumbsup:
